subject: Demo follow-up: recommended models, eval plan & QA monitoring
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>

Subject: Demo follow-up: recommended models, eval plan & QA monitoring

Hi Jordan / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap + next steps based on the signals you shared (customer-facing FAQ generation, short form product descriptions, and a downstream entity extraction pipeline for analytics):

Recommended shortlist (tradeoffs at a glance):
- retailco-model-s-quant (quantized 4-bit): lowest cost per token, p95 latency ~110–160ms at 1–4k concurrent QPS, best for bulk generation where cost matters. Slightly lower on very long-context coherency vs larger FP16 variants.
- retailco-model-m-fp16 (mid-size, FP16): balanced quality/cost, stronger on multi-sentence instructions and instruction-following; p95 latency ~180–240ms depending on sequence length.
- rerank-proto-1 (small reranker, CPU-offload): use as a post-filter for candidate lists to improve precision for product title selection and extraction; negligible latency added when batched.

Why these: they map to the three priorities you mentioned — throughput/cost sensitivity, a single higher-quality candidate for critical marketing copy, and a lightweight reranker for precision. Full rationale and benchmark snippets are in the attached latency_cost_matrix.xlsx and the Drive folder link below.

Eval assets attached/linked:
- retailco_prompt_set_v2.json (30 representative prompts across FAQs, descriptions, and extraction tasks)
- latency_cost_matrix.xlsx (p95 numbers from our internal bench with your target sequence lengths)
- eval-run-commands.sh (small test harness to reproduce the runs on our Hosted API)
- Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-retailco-evals

Quality/regression monitoring:
- We recommend establishing two alert tiers: (1) hard regression: >5% drop on your primary metric (ROUGE-L for descriptions / F1 for extraction) over a 24-hour rolling window; (2) soft drift: 1–5% drop flagged for inspection.
- Redwood Optimize can run daily evals against a pinned prompt set and send alerts + diffed outputs to a Slack channel and your S3 bucket.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm the primary evaluation metrics (F1 for extraction, BLEU/ROUGE for descriptions) and any locked prompt subsets from retailco_prompt_set_v2.json.
2) We run a 72-hour POC: two model variants (quant vs fp16) served on a small Dedicated pool using your sample traffic, Redwood runs the eval harness (we'll share the results dashboard).
3) Kickoff call to scope SSO/ingestion & pricing follow-up — propose Tue 2026-12-08 16:00 ET.

If these look good, Samir/Jordan can reply with any metric tweaks and whether you want us to include the reranker in the POC.

Thanks,
— Stephanie

Thanks Stephanie — very helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) Latency target: p95 < 200ms for our API-to-UI calls is critical for the ecommerce flow. Can your p95 numbers get consistently under that for the mid-size model if we limit max tokens to 128?
2) Regression concern: we’re worried about silent quality degradation after model updates — does Redwood support automatic rollback or can you trigger a fallback to an earlier pinned variant when alerts fire?
3) Compliance: the security team wants to confirm we can keep eval logs within our AWS account and that the POC won’t persist customer PII — is that doable?

If yes to all, please proceed with the 72-hour POC and include the reranker — we’ll provide a sample of real product titles for the extraction eval.

Hi Jordan — quick technical answers and a short plan to ensure we meet your p95 requirement and regression concerns.

On latency and model sizing:
- retailco-model-m-fp16: with a server-side prompt cap at 128 tokens and the same batching policy we demoed, we see p95 in the ~150–210ms band on A100-ish class hosts; numbers at the low end assume continuous batching and KV-cache warm. If you require strict <200ms p95 we can: (A) enable aggressive pre-warming and a short tail policy (keep n warm workers during peak windows), or (B) route interactive traffic to a lower-latency dedicated pool that costs more but hits ~140–180ms p95.

On automatic rollback / fallback:
- Redwood’s rollout mechanism supports automatic fallback to a pinned older model when a configured health check fails (you can define health in terms of latency or eval metrics). For the POC we recommend pinning retailco-model-m-fp16 as the primary and retailco-model-s-quant as the fallback. The control plane will switch at the route level — we can set the window to 5–15 minutes to avoid flapping.

On eval logs & PII:
- We can stream eval outputs and logs directly to your S3 bucket under a customer-managed prefix (no persistence on Redwood Hosted beyond ephemeral storage for the run).
- We’ll run an automatic redaction pass on the prompt set to hash/trim any PII fields unless you explicitly opt to retain raw examples for debugging.

Suggested eval framework (what we’ll run during 72-hour POC):
- Tasks: generation (descriptions), extraction (entity F1), reranking precision@5.
- Metrics: ROUGE-L & BLEU for long-form descriptions, micro-averaged F1 for extraction, precision@k for reranker.
- Thresholds: fail if primary metric drops >5% relative to baseline; warn at 1–5%.
- Frequency: daily baseline runs + continuous lightweight sampling (1% of traffic).

I’ve uploaded a small harness and a sample eval config to the Drive folder and attached eval-run-commands.sh to this thread. Steps for your engineering team to reproduce locally are in the script.

Let me know if you want us to include the SSO/SCIM checklist in the POC scope; we can add that to the kickoff agenda.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
